subject.title: Cron allows invalid Feishu announce jobs without delivery.to, causing runtime delivery failure

question: Should maintainers adopt one of the two open fork PRs that close this issue, or close them and allow a narrow replacement fix?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible and narrow, but duplicate open fork PRs already exist and are not directly maintainer-editable, so automation should not queue another PR until the landing path is chosen.

options.title: Adopt or refresh a fork PR
options.body: Review the two open fork PRs and ask for or create a maintainer-editable refresh of the cleaner candidate with gateway/service validation and regression coverage.

options.title: Close both and replace
options.body: Close the conflicting fork PRs and queue a new narrow fix PR that credits the prior attempts and preserves this issue as the canonical bug report.

options.title: Split UX follow-ups
options.body: Keep this issue scoped to create-time validation and open separate work only if maintainers want cron audit or clearer runtime diagnostics for legacy jobs.

recommendation.title: Adopt or refresh a fork PR
recommendation.body: Review the two open fork PRs and ask for or create a maintainer-editable refresh of the cleaner candidate with gateway/service validation and regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest recent history signal across cron service validation and outbound delivery cleanup, making him the best available owner for the landing-path choice.
